This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|

| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |

- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)

- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). - `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. ## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

230	权重上卡后，加载器要回答：**剩下的显存够不够跑？够的话怎么分？** Qwen3.5 的答案是一段顺序固定的预算计算，消费方有四个，优先级从高到低：
231	
232	1. **预填充 scratch**（GDR 分块内核的工作区）——不预留，长 prompt 预填充时会 OOM；
233	2. **recurrent 状态预留**——每个解码槽 2 份完整状态（图槽 + 一个在途 prefill 瞬态）；
234	3. **前缀快照槽**——由 `prefix_snapshot_bytes` 预算换算出的完整快照物理槽；
235	4. **KV 池**——拿剩余量的 85%，且不低于 64 页下限。
236	
237	「先扣除会 OOM 的，再分 KV」这个顺序本身就是注释里写明的正确性约定。任何一项不满足都在启动时 fail-fast，而不是服务中途崩溃。
238	
239	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
240	
241	预算计算的流程（全部发生在权重装载之后、KV 池分配之前）：
242	
243	```text
244	free_bytes = cuMemGetInfo()                        ← 权重上卡后的真实剩余
245	scratch_reserve    = GdrChunkwiseScratch35::estimate_bytes(config, geometry, 20_000)
246	recurrent_reserve  = 2 × 物理桶 × bytes_per_request(config, geometry)
247	snapshot_slots     = prefix_snapshot_bytes / bytes_per_request        ← 整数除法向下取整
248	snapshot_reserve   = snapshot_slots × bytes_per_request
249	门 1: prefix_snapshot_bytes > 0 时必须 snapshot_slots ≥ 1，否则拒绝启动
250	门 2: free ≥ scratch + recurrent + snapshot + 64 页最小 KV，否则拒绝启动
251	available = free − scratch − recurrent − snapshot
252	kv_budget = available × 0.85                       ← 留 15% 余量
253	num_pages  = max(kv_budget / bytes_per_page, 64)
254	```
255	
256	快照槽数换算的字节来源（分母）：
257	
258	\[
259	\text{bytes\_per\_request} = L_{\text{linear}} \times \big( \underbrace{H_v \times D_k \times D_v \times 4}_{\text{f32 递推状态}} + \underbrace{D_{qkv} \times (k_{\text{conv}} - 1) \times 2}_{\text{bf16 conv 状态}} \big)
260	\]
261	
262	其中 \(L_{\text{linear}}\) 是线性注意力层数，\(H_v\) 是本 rank 的 value 头数，\(D_k = D_v = 128\)，\(D_{qkv}\) 是本 rank 融合 qkv 维宽，\(k_{\text{conv}}\) 是卷积核宽（Qwen3.5 为 4，所以 conv 状态存 3 个历史输入）。

310	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
311	
312	**练习 1**：为什么 scratch 预留要放在 KV 池分配**之前**？如果反过来会发生什么？
313	
314	**答案**：KV 池按「剩余显存的 85%」贪心分配，几乎总能吃掉大头。若先分 KV，剩下的显存可能不够一次长 prompt 的 GDR 分块预填充工作区，服务会在运行中期预填充时 OOM 崩溃。先扣除 scratch（按 `SCRATCH_ESTIMATE_SEQ = 20_000` token 估算）再分 KV，把「启动时显式报错」替换掉「服务中途隐性崩溃」——fail-fast 原则在显存预算上的落点。
315	
316	**练习 2**：`STATES_PER_DECODE_SLOT = 2` 里的第二份状态是给谁的？
317	
318	**答案**：一份是解码槽自身的图槽状态（CUDA Graph 重放时 slot `i` 读写固定地址的那份），另一份是该解码槽在途 prefill 的瞬态状态——一个正在预填充的请求在分块推进期间需要一份独立工作状态，完成后才搬进图槽。预留按「每解码槽 2 份」计算，保证任何组合都不超额。
319	
320	**练习 3**：KV 池预算为什么取 `available × 0.85` 而不是 100%？
321	
322	**答案**：`cuMemGetInfo` 只报告当前空闲字节，运行期还有装载期未统计到的零散分配（CUDA Graph 捕获的工作区、NCCL 缓冲、驱动内部结构等）。留 15% 余量是对这些「看不见的消费者」的工程缓冲；同时 `MIN_KV_PAGES = 64` 保证极小显存下池子仍能开张（也是门 2 的 fail-fast 阈值的一部分）。

362	## 6. 本讲小结
363	
364	- 加载管线五步：分片索引（`load_shard_info_fixed`）→ advisory 预取（仅单 GPU）→ mmap → `SafeTensors` 零拷贝反序列化 → `WeightSource` 逐张量装载；四种装载路径（整取 / 行切 / 列切 / 多段拼接）覆盖全部权重。
365	- 装载即校验：每个分片装载都先对拍 checkpoint 与 config 的全局形状再切片，配置与权重不符在 loader 处 fail-fast，绝不流到 GEMM。
366	- 装载期融合：`in_proj_qkvz`（qkv 三段拼接 + z）、`in_proj_ba`、`gate_up_proj` 都在加载时 vstack 成形，把多次小 GEMM 合成一次；gated q_proj 的行切按头块对齐，保持每头 [q, gate] 相邻。
367	- `ModelRuntimeConfig` 携带四个运行时旋钮；`decode_admission_batch`（用户 `--max-batch`）与 `reserved_decode_slots`（`bucket_for` 取整的物理桶）分离是 #470 的结果——按物理桶分配缓冲、按请求值控制准入。
368	- `tie_word_embeddings` 两分支：tied 时 `lm_head = None` 且 `output_projection()` 回退 `embed_tokens`；untied 时加载顶层 `lm_head.weight`；两者都不参与 TP 切分。
369	- 显存预算四笔预留有固定顺序（prefill scratch → recurrent 状态 → 前缀快照 → KV 池 85%），`snapshot_slots = prefix_snapshot_bytes / bytes_per_request` 向下取整，非零预算换不出一个槽（4B 单槽 49.125 MiB）即拒绝启动。
370	
371	## 7. 下一步学习建议
372	
373	本讲完成后，`Qwen35Model` 已在 GPU 上组装完毕，但每个 `TransformerBlock35` 内部的前向还没展开。下一讲 **u2-l4「层结构：TransformerBlock35 与两种注意力层」**正好接上：`LayerKind` 如何按 `config.layer_types[i]` 分发、两种注意力层各自持有本讲已装载的哪些权重与几何维度。之后再进入 u3 单元深读两种层的前向与内核。建议顺带重读 [src/weights.rs:L322-L326](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights.rs#L322-L326) 的启动日志格式——以后每次拉起服务，这行日志就是检查显存预算是否合理的第一入口。

# 权重加载：safetensors、mmap 与 Qwen35Model 组装

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 完整描述一条权重从磁盘上的 safetensors 分片，到 GPU 上 `DeviceMatrix` / `DeviceVec` 的加载管线，并说出每一步由哪个函数负责。
2. 解释 `ModelRuntimeConfig` 的四个运行时旋钮（CUDA Graph、TP、设备序号、前缀快照预算）如何传入加载过程，以及 `decode_admission_batch` 与物理桶容量 `reserved_decode_slots` 为何要分开保存（issue #470）。
3. 手算 `prefix_snapshot_bytes` 如何除以单请求快照字节数得到快照槽数，并复现 Qwen3.5-4B「每请求 49.125 MiB」这个数。
4. 找出 `tie_word_embeddings` 两条分支各自的 lm_head 来源：Untied 时加载独立的 `lm_head.weight`，Tied 时直接复用 `embed_tokens`。
5. 整理出一份「权重名 → 结构体字段 → 是否按 shard 切分」的映射表（本讲综合实践）。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲假设你已读过前几讲，特别是：

- **u2-l1**：`config.json` 如何经 `RawConfig` → `Config35` 一次性校验；三个词表宽度（`vocab_size` / `decodable_vocab` / `selection_vocab`）各司其职。
- **u2-l2**：`LocalGeometry` 如何从 `Config35` + `TensorParallelConfig` 派生本 rank 的 `local_*` 维度，以及 `shard_range` 切分。
- **u1-l1**：Qwen3.5 是「全注意力 + Gated DeltaNet 线性注意力」混合架构，crate 内并存 KV cache 与 recurrent 状态两套系统。

再补三个本讲要用到的背景概念：

- **safetensors**：Hugging Face 推出的权重序列化格式。文件头部是一段 JSON 元数据（记录每个张量的名字、dtype、形状、字节偏移），之后是连续的原始数据。它不做压缩、布局可预测，所以适合直接 `mmap`。
- **mmap（内存映射文件）**：把文件「映射」进进程地址空间，访问内存就是访问磁盘内容，由操作系统按页懒加载。加载大权重时不必一次性 `read` 整个文件进堆内存。
- **显存预算（memory budgeting）**：加载完权重后，剩余显存要在「预填充 scratch、recurrent 状态、前缀快照、KV 池」四者之间分配。分配顺序本身就是一条正确性约定：先为会 OOM 的消费方预留，再把余量给 KV 池。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
|------|------|
| `src/weights.rs` | 本讲主线。`Qwen35Model` 结构体、`from_safetensors*` 三个构造函数、显存预算计算、KV 池与 pad 抑制的创建 |
| `src/weights/layers.rs` | 层容器类型（`TransformerBlock35`、`FullAttentionLayer`、`LinearAttentionLayer`、`MLP35`）与 `WeightSource`——权重名到结构体字段的映射全部在这里 |
| `pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs` | 跨模型共享的加载底座：分片索引解析、mmap、反序列化、预取线程、逐张量（含分片/拼接）装载 |
| `src/recurrent_state.rs` | `bytes_per_request`：一个请求的 recurrent/conv 快照字节数，是快照槽数换算的分母 |
| `src/batch_decode_graph.rs` | `BATCH_BUCKETS` / `MAX_BATCH` / `bucket_for`：物理解码容量的取整规则 |
| `src/lib.rs` | `Qwen35LaunchOptions.prefix_cache_mib` → `prefix_snapshot_bytes` 的 MiB 换算，以及对 `from_safetensors` 的调用点 |
| `Cargo.toml` | 依赖声明：`safetensors`、`pegainfer-core` 等；`qwen35 = ["pegainfer-kernels/qwen35"]` 的 feature 转发 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

本讲拆成三个最小模块：**safetensors mmap**（权重怎么进来）、**运行时配置**（加载时受什么控制）、**显存预算**（剩余显存怎么分）。

### 4.1 模块一：safetensors mmap——从分片文件到 GPU 张量

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

一个 Qwen3.5 checkpoint 通常被切成若干个 `*.safetensors` 分片，外加一个 `model.safetensors.index.json` 索引文件，说明「每个张量住在哪个分片里」。加载要解决三件事：

1. **找到张量**：名字 → 分片文件的定位；
2. **不撑爆内存**：用 mmap 让操作系统按需把文件页搬进来，而不是把整个文件读进堆；
3. **校验形状**：张量的真实形状必须与 `config.json` 声明一致，且分片切片范围合法——错误要在装载时爆掉，而不是留到 GEMM 里。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

加载管线的五步（对应下文源码精读）：

```text
① load_shard_info_fixed   读 index.json → (分片路径列表, weight_map: 名字→分片序号)
        │                 （单文件 checkpoint 直接返回那一个文件）
② WeightPrefetch::spawn   仅单 GPU：开 8 个线程做 advisory 预取，把文件页提前读进 page cache
③ mmap_shards             每个分片 mmap 进地址空间
④ deserialize_shards      在每个 mmap 上解析 safetensors 头 → SafeTensors 视图（零拷贝借用 mmap）
⑤ WeightSource 逐张量装载  按 config 声明的形状整取 / 行切 / 列切 / 多段拼接 → DeviceMatrix/DeviceVec
```

其中第 ⑤ 步有四种装载路径：

| 路径 | 函数 | 语义 |
|------|------|------|
| 整取 | `tensor_2d` / `tensor_1d` | 不切分，全量上传（embed、lm_head、norm 等） |
| 行切 | `row_shard_if_needed` | 取全局矩阵的第 `[offset, offset+len)` 行（TP 下输出维度分片） |
| 列切 | `col_shard_if_needed` | 取列分片（TP 下 o_proj / down_proj / out_proj 这类「输入侧」分片） |
| 拼接 | `linear_in_proj_qkv` / `linear_conv1d` / `load_tensor_2d_row_stitch` | 从全局张量的**多个段**各取本 rank 的局部行，拼成一个连续矩阵 |

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**第一步：解析分片索引。** 单文件 checkpoint 走捷径，返回空的 `weight_map`；分片 checkpoint 解析 `index.json` 的 `weight_map`，把每个张量名映射到分片列表下标：

- [pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs:L57-L89](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs#L57-L89) —— `load_shard_info`：先探测 `model.safetensors` 单文件是否存在；否则读 `model.safetensors.index.json`，遍历 `weight_map` 构建「张量名 → 分片下标」。`load_shard_info_fixed`（[L1055 起](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs#L1055)）在其上追加一层文件名修正：索引里写的 `model.safetensors-00001-...` 在磁盘上不存在时，尝试改成 `model-00001-...` 再探一次。
- 查询侧的兜底在 [pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs:L331-L349](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs#L331-L349) —— `find_tensor`：`weight_map` 命中就直接取对应分片；否则（单文件场景 `weight_map` 为空）逐个分片试一遍。这解释了为什么单文件路径可以返回空 map。

**第二、三、四步：预取、mmap、反序列化。** 在模型构造函数里按顺序发生：

- [src/weights.rs:L186-L190](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights.rs#L186-L190) —— `weights.rs` 的调用点：`load_shard_info_fixed` 拿到 `(shard_paths, weight_map)`；`WeightPrefetch::spawn` **只在 `world_size == 1` 时启动**；随后 `mmap_shards` + `deserialize_shards`。
- [pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs:L301-L319](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs#L301-L319) —— `mmap_shards`：对每个分片 `unsafe { Mmap::map(&file) }`。安全性注释写明约定：**Mmap 在整个加载期间保持存活，且文件不会被并发修改**。
- [pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs:L322-L329](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs#L322-L329) —— `deserialize_shards`：在每个 mmap 上 `SafeTensors::deserialize`，得到借用 mmap 字节的视图集合，后续按张量名取 `TensorView` 都是零拷贝。
- [pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs:L91-L100](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs#L91-L100) 与 [L142-L149](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs#L142-L149) —— `WeightPrefetch`：文档注释明说这是 **advisory（建议性）** 预取——loader 从不依赖它；Drop 时取消并 join 工作线程，失败聚合成一条警告。它按 16 MiB 一个 chunk 把文件分给 8 个线程读，还有「预取速率低于 1 GiB/s 就放弃」的自适应门槛（`FLOOR_BYTES_PER_SEC`）。在 [src/weights.rs:L250-L255](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights.rs#L250-L255)，`ctx.sync()` 之后 `drop(prefetch)` —— 权重全部上卡了，预取才功成身退。

**第五步：WeightSource 逐张量装载。** `WeightSource` 是「一次模型加载的张量来源 + 各层 loader 共用的 TP 切分范围」：

- [src/weights/layers.rs:L224-L249](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights/layers.rs#L224-L249) —— `WeightSource` 结构体：持有 `ctx`、`shards`、`weight_map`、`geometry`，以及一组预计算好的 `Shard`（`gated_q`、`q_cols`、`kv_rows`、`intermediate`、`linear_value_heads`、`linear_z`）。注释点明设计意图：**config 与 checkpoint 不符时，要在 loader 处停下，而不是让错误流到一个按 config 尺寸分配的 GEMM 里**。
- [src/weights/layers.rs:L196-L211](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights/layers.rs#L196-L211) —— `Shard` 把「本 rank 的 `(offset, len)`」和「切分前的全局长度」绑成一对，调用方无法拿 A 维度的范围去配 B 维度的全局长度。
- [src/weights/layers.rs:L285-L300](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights/layers.rs#L285-L300) —— `row_shard_if_needed`：TP 分片时走 `load_tensor_2d_row_shard`（带行偏移与全局形状断言），TP1 时退化为整取。
- [pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs:L817-L834](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs#L817-L834) —— `load_tensor_2d_row_shard`：`ensure_global_shape`（对拍 checkpoint 与 config）→ `check_row_range`（切片不越界）→ 在宿主侧切出 `[start..end]` 的 bf16 元素 → `DeviceMatrix::from_host` 一次上传。这就是「先校验后变更」：任何不符都在这一步报错。
- [src/weights/layers.rs:L338-L350](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights/layers.rs#L338-L350) —— `linear_in_proj_qkv`：融合 qkv 不能一刀切。checkpoint 里是 `[全部 q 行 | 全部 k 行 | 全部 v 行]` 三段，本 rank 要从**每段里**各取自己的头部局部行，再拼成 `[q_local | k_local | v_local]`，用 `load_tensor_2d_row_stitch` 完成。为什么不能跨段重排？[L386-L407](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights/layers.rs#L386-L407) 的注释一针见血：**q 行按 key heads 计数、v 行按 value heads 计数，两者的 shard 边界不一样**（gated-q 教训）。单测 [L474-L491](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights/layers.rs#L474-L491) 给了 TP2 下的具体数字：q=k=2048、v=4096、全局 8192 行，rank0 取 `[(0,1024),(2048,1024),(4096,2048)]`，rank1 取 `[(1024,1024),(3072,1024),(6144,2048)]`，两 rank 的段拼起来严丝合缝覆盖 `[0,8192)`。
- [src/weights/layers.rs:L369-L383](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights/layers.rs#L369-L383) 与 [L421-L431](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights/layers.rs#L421-L431) —— `gated_q_proj`：全注意力的 q_proj 每个头带一个输出门，行布局是「每个头先 `head_dim` 行 q、紧跟 `head_dim` 行 gate」。所以 TP 切分按**头块**切而不是平切行区间，保证本 rank 每个头的 q 行与 gate 行相邻。

**装载时的两处融合。** Qwen3.5 的 checkpoint 把线性注意力的四个投影分开存，加载时 fusion 成两个矩阵，注释明说这是对齐 vLLM 的做法、让每组一次 GEMM 而不是四次 launch：

- [src/weights/layers.rs:L153-L168](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights/layers.rs#L153-L168) —— `in_proj_qkv` 与 `in_proj_z` 各自装载后 `DeviceMatrix::vstack` 成 `in_proj_qkvz`；`in_proj_b` 与 `in_proj_a` 同样拼成 `in_proj_ba`（beta 占低行、alpha 占高行，见 [L36-L39](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights/layers.rs#L36-L39) 结构体注释）。
- [src/weights/layers.rs:L88-L99](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights/layers.rs#L88-L99) —— MLP 同理：`gate_proj` 与 `up_proj` 行切后 vstack 成 `gate_up_proj`（SwiGLU 的经典融合），`down_proj` 列切。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践：读索引、走一遍名字定位

**实践目标**：把「张量名 → 分片 → TensorView」这条链在纸面上走通。

**操作步骤**：

1. 打开任一个本地 safetensors checkpoint 目录（没有的话，直接读下面代码也行）：看是否存在 `model.safetensors`（单文件）或 `model.safetensors.index.json` + 多个分片。
2. 若有 `index.json`，用 `jq '.weight_map | to_entries[:5]' model.safetensors.index.json`（或文本编辑器搜索）看前 5 条映射，确认张量名的格式是 `model.language_model.layers.0.*`。
3. 对照 [pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs:L331-L349](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-core/src/weight_loader.rs#L331-L349) 的 `find_tensor` 回答：名字 `model.language_model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight` 在分片场景下经过几次哈希查找、几次文件访问？（答案：一次 map 查找拿到分片下标，一次 `shards[idx].tensor(name)`。）
4. 再看 [src/weights.rs:L186-L190](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights.rs#L186-L190)，注意 `WeightPrefetch::spawn` 外面套着 `(geometry.world_size() == 1).then(...)`。

**需要观察的现象 / 预期结果**（无 checkpoint 时为纸面推导，标注待本地验证的部分）：

- 单文件 checkpoint：`weight_map` 为空，`find_tensor` 走逐分片扫描的兜底分支（本例只有一个分片，等价于直接取）。
- 分片 checkpoint：每个名字先查 map，O(1) 定位分片。
- 预取线程只在单 GPU 启动；TP 场景下这一步是 `None`。预取失败不会让加载失败，只会打一条警告。`jq` 命令的输出格式：待本地验证（取决于是否有本地 checkpoint）。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `mmap_shards` 里的 `Mmap` 对象必须活到所有权重装载完成？如果提前 drop 会怎样？

**答案**：`deserialize_shards` 返回的 `SafeTensors` 视图是**零拷贝借用** mmap 字节的——`TensorView` 指向的就是映射页里的数据。mmap 对象被 drop 后映射解除，后续任何通过视图读数据的操作都会解引用失效映射（未定义行为/崩溃）。代码用生命周期 `SafeTensors<'a>` 让编译器强制这一点，`weights.rs` 中 `mmaps` 与 `shards` 在整个构造函数里同存活域，`ctx.sync()` 之后才一起释放。

**练习 2**：TP=2 时，`in_proj_qkv` 为什么不能像普通行切那样取一个连续区间 `[offset, offset+len)`？

**答案**：因为 checkpoint 布局是 `[q 全部行 | k 全部行 | v 全部行]` 三段拼接，而 q/k 行数按 key heads 计算、v 行数按 value heads 计算，TP 切分后每段里本 rank 的局部起点各不相同。若取一个平切区间，会横跨段边界，把别的 rank 的 q 行混进本 rank 的 v 区。正确做法是每段各取局部行再拼接（`load_tensor_2d_row_stitch` + 三段 range），单测 `linear_qkv_shard_segments_stitch_head_local_slices` 正是验证三段拼起来无缝覆盖全局。

**练习 3**：`gated_q_proj` 的行切分与 `k_proj` 的行切分有什么本质区别？

**答案**：`k_proj` 是平切——全局 `kv_dim` 行均分给各 rank，一个 `(offset, len)` 就够。`gated_q_proj` 的行是「每头 `[q; gate]` 成对相邻」，rank 边界必须落在头边界上，所以 offset 按 `rank × local_heads × head_dim × 2` 计算，保证每个头的 q 行和 gate 行不被拆开。

### 4.2 模块二：运行时配置——ModelRuntimeConfig 与构造函数家族

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

权重装载不是纯函数：同一份 checkpoint，根据「要不要 CUDA Graph、跑在哪个 GPU、TP 第几个 rank、给前缀快照留多少显存」会装载出不同的 `Qwen35Model`。这些旋钮打包成 `ModelRuntimeConfig`。本模块还要讲清一个容易被忽略的分离：**调度器准入上限（`decode_admission_batch`）与物理解码容量（`reserved_decode_slots`）不是同一个数**——前者是用户请求的 `--max-batch`，后者向上取整到 CUDA Graph 批次桶。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
CLI / 启动选项
    │  --max-batch=N（1..=64）
    ▼
from_safetensors_with_runtime_and_capacity(model_path, runtime, max_batch)
    ├─ 校验 max_batch ∈ 1..=MAX_BATCH(64)，否则报错
    ├─ decode_admission_batch = max_batch          ← 保留用户请求
    ├─ max_batch = bucket_for(max_batch)           ← 取整到 {1,2,4,8,16,32,64}
    │    （例：--max-batch 5 → 物理桶 8，准入仍是 5）
    ├─ DeviceContext::new_with_device(runtime.device_ordinal)
    ├─ Config35::from_file + LocalGeometry::try_new   ← u2-l1 / u2-l2 的边界
    ├─ bound_selection_vocab(decodable_vocab)          ← u2-l1 的词表宽度
    ├─ … 权重装载（模块一）…
    └─ 显存预算与 KV 池（模块三）
```

`bucket_for` 的取整规则：从小到大扫 `{1,2,4,8,16,32,64}`，返回第一个 `>= bs` 的桶。

### 4.3 模块三：显存预算——四笔预留与 prefix_snapshot_bytes → 槽数

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

权重上卡后，加载器要回答：**剩下的显存够不够跑？够的话怎么分？** Qwen3.5 的答案是一段顺序固定的预算计算，消费方有四个，优先级从高到低：

1. **预填充 scratch**（GDR 分块内核的工作区）——不预留，长 prompt 预填充时会 OOM；
2. **recurrent 状态预留**——每个解码槽 2 份完整状态（图槽 + 一个在途 prefill 瞬态）；
3. **前缀快照槽**——由 `prefix_snapshot_bytes` 预算换算出的完整快照物理槽；
4. **KV 池**——拿剩余量的 85%，且不低于 64 页下限。

「先扣除会 OOM 的，再分 KV」这个顺序本身就是注释里写明的正确性约定。任何一项不满足都在启动时 fail-fast，而不是服务中途崩溃。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

预算计算的流程（全部发生在权重装载之后、KV 池分配之前）：

```text
free_bytes = cuMemGetInfo()                        ← 权重上卡后的真实剩余
scratch_reserve    = GdrChunkwiseScratch35::estimate_bytes(config, geometry, 20_000)
recurrent_reserve  = 2 × 物理桶 × bytes_per_request(config, geometry)
snapshot_slots     = prefix_snapshot_bytes / bytes_per_request        ← 整数除法向下取整
snapshot_reserve   = snapshot_slots × bytes_per_request
门 1: prefix_snapshot_bytes > 0 时必须 snapshot_slots ≥ 1，否则拒绝启动
门 2: free ≥ scratch + recurrent + snapshot + 64 页最小 KV，否则拒绝启动
available = free − scratch − recurrent − snapshot
kv_budget = available × 0.85                       ← 留 15% 余量
num_pages  = max(kv_budget / bytes_per_page, 64)
```

快照槽数换算的字节来源（分母）：

\[
\text{bytes\_per\_request} = L_{\text{linear}} \times \big( \underbrace{H_v \times D_k \times D_v \times 4}_{\text{f32 递推状态}} + \underbrace{D_{qkv} \times (k_{\text{conv}} - 1) \times 2}_{\text{bf16 conv 状态}} \big)
\]

其中 \(L_{\text{linear}}\) 是线性注意力层数，\(H_v\) 是本 rank 的 value 头数，\(D_k = D_v = 128\)，\(D_{qkv}\) 是本 rank 融合 qkv 维宽，\(k_{\text{conv}}\) 是卷积核宽（Qwen3.5 为 4，所以 conv 状态存 3 个历史输入）。

**练习 1**：为什么 scratch 预留要放在 KV 池分配**之前**？如果反过来会发生什么？

**答案**：KV 池按「剩余显存的 85%」贪心分配，几乎总能吃掉大头。若先分 KV，剩下的显存可能不够一次长 prompt 的 GDR 分块预填充工作区，服务会在运行中期预填充时 OOM 崩溃。先扣除 scratch（按 `SCRATCH_ESTIMATE_SEQ = 20_000` token 估算）再分 KV，把「启动时显式报错」替换掉「服务中途隐性崩溃」——fail-fast 原则在显存预算上的落点。

**练习 2**：`STATES_PER_DECODE_SLOT = 2` 里的第二份状态是给谁的？

**答案**：一份是解码槽自身的图槽状态（CUDA Graph 重放时 slot `i` 读写固定地址的那份），另一份是该解码槽在途 prefill 的瞬态状态——一个正在预填充的请求在分块推进期间需要一份独立工作状态，完成后才搬进图槽。预留按「每解码槽 2 份」计算，保证任何组合都不超额。

**练习 3**：KV 池预算为什么取 `available × 0.85` 而不是 100%？

**答案**：`cuMemGetInfo` 只报告当前空闲字节，运行期还有装载期未统计到的零散分配（CUDA Graph 捕获的工作区、NCCL 缓冲、驱动内部结构等）。留 15% 余量是对这些「看不见的消费者」的工程缓冲；同时 `MIN_KV_PAGES = 64` 保证极小显存下池子仍能开张（也是门 2 的 fail-fast 阈值的一部分）。

**实践目标**：产出一 cheat-sheet 表，给定任意 `index.json` 里的张量名，能立刻说出它落到哪个字段、是否切分、走哪条装载路径。

## 6. 本讲小结

- 加载管线五步：分片索引（`load_shard_info_fixed`）→ advisory 预取（仅单 GPU）→ mmap → `SafeTensors` 零拷贝反序列化 → `WeightSource` 逐张量装载；四种装载路径（整取 / 行切 / 列切 / 多段拼接）覆盖全部权重。
- 装载即校验：每个分片装载都先对拍 checkpoint 与 config 的全局形状再切片，配置与权重不符在 loader 处 fail-fast，绝不流到 GEMM。
- 装载期融合：`in_proj_qkvz`（qkv 三段拼接 + z）、`in_proj_ba`、`gate_up_proj` 都在加载时 vstack 成形，把多次小 GEMM 合成一次；gated q_proj 的行切按头块对齐，保持每头 [q, gate] 相邻。
- `ModelRuntimeConfig` 携带四个运行时旋钮；`decode_admission_batch`（用户 `--max-batch`）与 `reserved_decode_slots`（`bucket_for` 取整的物理桶）分离是 #470 的结果——按物理桶分配缓冲、按请求值控制准入。
- `tie_word_embeddings` 两分支：tied 时 `lm_head = None` 且 `output_projection()` 回退 `embed_tokens`；untied 时加载顶层 `lm_head.weight`；两者都不参与 TP 切分。
- 显存预算四笔预留有固定顺序（prefill scratch → recurrent 状态 → 前缀快照 → KV 池 85%），`snapshot_slots = prefix_snapshot_bytes / bytes_per_request` 向下取整，非零预算换不出一个槽（4B 单槽 49.125 MiB）即拒绝启动。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

本讲完成后，`Qwen35Model` 已在 GPU 上组装完毕，但每个 `TransformerBlock35` 内部的前向还没展开。下一讲 **u2-l4「层结构：TransformerBlock35 与两种注意力层」**正好接上：`LayerKind` 如何按 `config.layer_types[i]` 分发、两种注意力层各自持有本讲已装载的哪些权重与几何维度。之后再进入 u3 单元深读两种层的前向与内核。建议顺带重读 [src/weights.rs:L322-L326](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights.rs#L322-L326) 的启动日志格式——以后每次拉起服务，这行日志就是检查显存预算是否合理的第一入口。

schema.name: Agent
schema.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.
